title: Home truths
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-quality original website concept sketch, landscape 1536x1024. NZ first-home buyer education, adult beginner, big explanatory imagery and very few words. Direction: bold independent editorial magazine, cut-paper photographic collage, oversized condensed black sans typography, vivid lemon yellow and cobalt blue, sharp asymmetric composition, confident Swiss-influenced layout. Not a dashboard or a beige handbook. Show one full desktop screen, no devices, no external presentation board.
Top narrow white masthead: "HOME TRUTHS" left, "Start here   All topics   Search" right. Main canvas yellow. Huge headline top-left "The price isn't the whole price." Occupies upper-left with confident line breaks. Large central/right visual metaphor: realistic cutout small New Zealand weatherboard house sitting atop a huge folded shopping receipt. Distinct cutout objects arranged along the receipt: keys, lawyer's folder, building inspection torch, rain gutter, insurance umbrella. Small clean black labels on separate white paper strips: "Buying costs", "Ongoing costs", "Repair buffer". Composition explains layers of costs without specific monetary amounts. Use purposeful collage, halftone texture sparingly, ample reading space; no dense paragraph. Large cobalt action button bottom-left "Unpack the costs →", small secondary "Show me a real example". Bottom white persistent navigator with 5 short links "Decide   Prepare   Find   Buy   Own", Prepare selected by black underline, and "02 / 05". Small visible footer link "Gotchas + official links". Expressive fresh adult editorial art, polished imagery, crisp readable type. No vintage engraving, serif headlines, rounded card grids, floating neon UI, dense annotations or 3D game world. This is an original design informed by general editorial collage principles, do not copy any artist's artwork.

title: The money lab
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one landscape 1536x1024 original NZ first-home buyer educational website screen concept. This direction is a playful physical experiment, radically unlike an editorial magazine, article, dashboard or illustrated world. Midnight navy background, white precise grotesk typography, bright tangerine and ice-blue translucent objects. Sparse high-end industrial design, centered composition with tons of negative space. Premium rendered tactile 3D model with soft restrained lighting, diagram precision, no expensive magical effects.
Header left "HOME LAB" right "Experiments   My notes   All topics". Center top small "02 · YOUR MONTHLY MONEY", large heading "What is left after the house?" and one tiny line "Move the costs. See the trade-off."
Central scene a large horizontal physical budget tray, built of beautiful matte geometric blocks: orange house-shaped block for "Mortgage", smaller blue blocks "Rates", "Insurance", "Upkeep", a final EMPTY transparent compartment labeled "Money left". Blocks all share same baseline and comparable widths. It is a conceptual teaching model without fake numerical answers. Labels crisp and outside objects; dotted guides visually connect each label to block. Beneath the tray a single horizontal slider labeled "Home cost" with "Less" and "More" at ends, and a simple reset icon. Lower region a prominent white sentence "The mortgage is only one piece." Below two restrained text buttons "What's included? +" and "Assumptions + sources".
Fixed bottom slim progress line "Decide — Money — Search — Offer — Move", Money highlighted orange. Left "← Back", right white rectangular button "Next experiment →". Make the whole screen look like a quiet interactive exhibit that invites one action, not fintech account balances or gaming HUD. No sidebars, card grids, charts with numbers, coins, purple gradients, mascots, parchment, ornamental motion. Concept sketch for adult novices with accurate short English text.

title: One buyer's story
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a landscape 1536x1024 concept sketch of a browser-based interactive graphic novel for NZ first-home buyers. Entire composition is a sophisticated illustrated comic, flat screenprinted color, thick confident ink contour, expressive adult characters, coral red, turquoise and pale peach, off-white gutters. Geometric friendly sans lettering, NOT realistic render, photo collage, beige engraved guide, SaaS UI, or game-world map. One browser screen no mockup frame. Clear three-panel sequential layout left-to-right, then a wide clean decision band across bottom. Strong differing panel sizes and real comic rhythm. Title top "OUR FIRST PLACE" with compact "Episodes   Jump to a topic   Saved" links.
Episode heading "03 / The house we nearly rushed into".
Panel 1 narrow: young adult buyer and partner approach a welcoming modest weatherboard house, holding open-home flyer. Brief speech bubble "This could be it."
Panel 2 widest: interior room with same two people, one looking up at a visible brown ceiling stain. Close focus makes the stain obvious, small bubble "What's that mark?"
Panel 3 narrow: partner holding phone to call an inspector, dialogue "Let's find out first."
Bottom large white decision band, headline "You spot a stain. What next?" two very clear rectangular choices with ample space: "Ask what caused it" and "Arrange an inspection". Under choices small text "Explore either path. Nothing is a test." Small link "What the checks can miss +" and "Official guidance ↗".
Persistent page arrows bottom-left and bottom-right; tiny 5-stage text trail "Decide · Prepare · Search · Offer · Move" with Search selected; no forced linear lock. Imagery explains a memorable real decision, no lengthy paragraphs and no multiple sprawling buttons over faces. The comic is adult, warm, humorous in humanity but not silly. High-quality consistent original illustration. Short text exact and readable. Make this feel like a beautifully art-directed digital comic with branching decisions, not a conventional website with illustration on one side.

title: The viewing companion
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a 1536x1024 landscape concept sketch for a radically practical photo-led NZ first-home buyer learning product named "LOOK CLOSER". Visual direction: premium documentary photography, deep forest green, clean white, signal yellow annotations, large sturdy sans typography. No illustrated cartoon characters, no engraving, no collage paper texture, no 3D game world. Asymmetrical mobile-first field guide shown as a desktop working surface, no actual device frames.
Composition: left two-thirds huge natural-light photographic interior of an ordinary NZ home, looking towards an older timber window; window has visible condensation and small area of discoloured timber sill, subtle reality, not dramatic damage. A single small yellow numbered ring "1" with thin leader points to the sill, doesn't cover detail. Above image white heading "A closer look at the window." and small breadcrumb "SEARCH / AT A VIEWING". Photo has three clean thumbnail crops along bottom edge marked "Windows", "Ceiling", "Outside", Windows selected with yellow line.
Right third is solid WHITE reading area integrated edge-to-edge no floating cards, large dark green type with generous margins. Small "CHECK 1 OF 6", headline "See damp? Ask why." Two very short rows "Look for: staining and soft timber." and "Ask: has this been repaired?" A pale yellow note strip "A photo cannot tell you the cause." Then two large readable buttons "Save a question" and "Next check →". Lower down plain expandable links "Who can check this? +" and "Guidance + useful links ↗". No dense disclaimer text.
Full-width top forest header with white "LOOK CLOSER" left and "My stage   All topics   Saved" right. Bottom persistent forest footer "Plan   Money   Viewings   Offer   Move", Viewings in yellow. Photo is an AI-generated illustrative example not a real inspected property. Credible, visually immediate, calm hierarchy, clear user task. This is a design sketch communicating how contextual photography can teach people what to notice and ask, not diagnosing buildings.
